ENOCH SCROLL

LET THEM — WHEN LOVE LEARNS TO RELEASE

God gave us free will. Why deny it to those we love?

When a loved one walks contrary to God’s Word, we witness, warn, pray, and plead.

When they won’t listen, we try harder.

When does guiding someone toward God become trying to do His work?

THE GOD WHO LETS US CHOOSE

Reflecting on “Let Them,” I realized God has allowed humanity to choose from the beginning.

He knew we would wander and make painful choices. Yet He gave us free will.

Not from indifference, but because forced love is not freely given.

In Deuteronomy 30:19, God sets life and death before us and urges us to choose life.

He reveals truth and consequences, but leaves the choice.

What an extraordinary expression of love.

WE ARE WITNESSES, NOT SAVIORS

Witnessing through the Holy Spirit is not the same as taking responsibility for someone’s transformation.

When Jesus spoke to the rich young ruler, He told him the truth. The man walked away sorrowful.

And Jesus let him walk.

He did not force obedience.

If Jesus allowed him to choose, why do we struggle to give those we love the same freedom?

Perhaps love becomes entangled with fear: of their pain, mistakes, or loss.

But the Holy Spirit does not need us to become Him.

LOVE THAT RELEASES

The prodigal son’s father let him leave, though hardship might follow.

The son lost everything and knew hunger.

Then Scripture says:

“And when he came to himself…” — Luke 15:17

There was the awakening.

Not because his father argued, but because he recognized truth for himself.

And when he returned, his father welcomed him with open arms.

The father released his son’s choices without releasing his love.

PLANT THE SEED. RELEASE THE HARVEST.

“I have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase.” — 1 Corinthians 3:6

How often do we plant a seed, then dig it up to check its growth?

We plead and question, frustrated by no visible change.

But transformation is not always visible. We may plant. Someone else may water. The growth belongs to God.

Faith can mean stepping aside and trusting His harvest.

LET THEM — BUT NEVER STOP LOVING THEM

“Let them” does not mean approving of sin, abandoning biblical truth, tolerating abuse, or failing to protect someone in danger.

It means understanding where our responsibility ends and another person’s freedom begins.

We can disagree without condemning, set boundaries with love, and pray without controlling.

Loved ones may walk through valleys we wish they could avoid.

Yet valleys can become classrooms, even opportunities for awakening.

THE GREATER SURRENDER

Perhaps the hardest person to surrender to God is someone we love.

We pray for changed hearts, then rise and try through pressure what we asked God to do through His Spirit.

But what if surrender also means allowing God to change us?

To quiet fear, soften frustration, and release control?

Perhaps the greatest act of faith is not convincing someone to change, but trusting God enough to release our need to change them.

Speak the truth.
Plant the seeds.
Pray without ceasing.
Then trust God with the harvest.

Let them choose.
Let them learn.
Let them encounter God for themselves.

And let God do what only God can do.

Releasing control is not surrendering hope. God can work even when we cannot see it.

We were never called to be someone else’s Holy Spirit.

We were called to be vessels of His love.

PRAYER OF SURRENDER

Heavenly Father,

Forgive me when my love becomes fear and my concern becomes control. Give me wisdom to know when to speak and when to be silent.

I release those I’ve tried to change into Your hands. Let the seeds grow in Your time.

As You work in their hearts, work in mine.

Teach me to let them choose, while I choose to trust You.

In Jesus’ name, Amen.

ENOCH SCROLLS
Reflections on Faith, Surrender, and Spiritual Awakening
